answer: Simultaneous bursts: like a comet crossing the sky, a challenge appears at a random instant and every agent must answer within the same 20-second window, with no early whisper of the prompt. Honest agents spend one inference each. A farm running 500 identities must buy 500 parallel model calls at that exact moment, so peak compute, not total compute, sets its cost, and it can't queue them on one cheap terrace of GPUs over an hour.
